gen-dafont-amadeus-switzer: Amadeus stretches its words wide across the line, round letters upright with no tilt in the stress. Switzer takes over below, tubular and wire-like with a tall waist line, a quieter partner to all that stretch.
gen-dafont-capture-it-fs-asap: Tall, tight and urban: Capture It has a towering x-height and openings so slight its letters feel nearly sealed. And Asap sets open arcs against that sealed heading, the sharpest split in the pair.
gen-dafont-capture-it-fs-epilogue: Commanding and urban, Capture It towers with a huge x-height. Epilogue's curvy, unclamped letters stay open exactly where the heading stays nearly sealed, and that split carries the whole pairing.
gen-dafont-capture-it-general-sans: Urban and commanding, Capture It piles up a towering x-height with letters that feel nearly sealed. And where the heading hits hard, General Sans keeps a steady pen pressure that lets the lines run smoothly on.
gen-dafont-capture-it-switzer: Switzer reads tubular and approachable, with a tall waist line. Capture It, towering and nearly sealed, meets c tips that never close in, and that split is the strongest thing here.
gen-dafont-existence-fs-asap: Wide glass portholes for counters give Existence its look, with terminals cut well short of the bowl. And Asap keeps paragraphs moving, its open arcs and near-capital body height making text feel readable line after line.
gen-dafont-existence-fs-epilogue: Epilogue brings curvy, unclamped letters to the page. Existence's porthole counters and cut-short terminals stay up top, while the tall-bodied, stubby-ascender text below keeps an approachable, contemporary feel through every line.
gen-dafont-existence-fs-public-sans: Strokes of uniform mass and wide glass-porthole counters give Existence its industrial look, with terminals cut short of the bowl. Public Sans reads sturdy and trustworthy, broad counters welcoming the eye.
gen-dafont-existence-general-sans: General Sans keeps a steady pen pressure throughout. Existence is the one to make a statement with its porthole counters, while General Sans fills the line, its bends smooth and unobstructed.
gen-dafont-lemon-milk-fs-asap: Lemon Milk spreads its loose, wide tracking across rounded letters drawn with a single-width, rolling-ball-pen line. Asap can drop to a modest size, since its body height nearly matches the capitals.
